brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Three hex base cells in a row (piece at q=-1,0,1 r=0) form the rack, with a keyhole hanger (hex-acc-keyhole) on the same face of each cell, so it is designed to hang on screws already in a wall. The configurator does not check the wall or screw spacing.
Three Bin, full depth (hex-bin-full) trays, one in each base cell at q=-1, 0 and 1.
Three keyhole hangers (accessory hex-acc-keyhole) at slot 1 of each cell. Caps closed the remaining open faces and joints are bolted (lockJoints). check_build: no issues, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Suitable for storing spices (food-safe, material, moisture)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit only; it does not judge food safety or material. The user must choose a food-safe printing material.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell wall-hung spice rack: three full hex bases in a row, each with a full-depth bin and a keyhole hanger on the same face, with open faces capped and joints bolted. check_build is clean (meshClash clear). Mounting needs matching screws in the wall; the material's food safety is not checked here.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
